```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

This vignette lists the **other** datasets shipped with **interactmeta**.
The CAMS workflow (subgroup pairs, information fractions, **`cams()`**,
**`forestplot()`**) is developed on **`steroids`** (IV / NIV) in
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html). Here we only note disease context,
subgroup labels, and effect scale.

```{r load-interactmeta, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(interactmeta)
library(dplyr)
```

| Dataset | Setting | Subgroups | Effect on `yi` scale |
|---------|---------|-----------|----------------------|
| `age` | MS immunotherapies; relapse | Younger, Older | Log incidence-rate ratio |
| `edss` | Same review; relapse | Lower, Higher EDSS | Log incidence-rate ratio |
| `il6` | IL-6 antagonists, COVID-19 mortality | Corticosteroids yes / no | Log odds ratio from counts |
| `respire_age` | RESPIRE bronchiectasis; time to exacerbation | `<65`, `>=65` | Log hazard ratio |
| `respire_sex` | Same trials | Female, Male | Log hazard ratio |

**`age`** and **`edss`** follow @heesen2024; **`il6`** follows
@stern2021il6; **`respire_age`** and **`respire_sex`** follow
@desoyza2018respire1 and @aksamit2018respire2.

## Multiple sclerosis: `age`

Published log rate ratios are already in **`yi`** / **`vi`**. CONFIRM
arms are split as **`CONFIRM-B`** and **`CONFIRM-C`**.

```{r age-head}
age |>
  select(study, subgroup, treatment, yi, vi) |>
  head()
```

```{r age-fit, cache = TRUE}
age_es <- escalc(measure = "IRR", yi = yi, vi = vi, data = age)
fit_age <- cams(
  age_es,
  reference = "Younger",
  method = "REML"
)
```

```{r age-forest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
forestplot(fit_age, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## Multiple sclerosis: `edss`

Same review as **`age`**, EDSS strata instead of age.

```{r edss-head}
edss |>
  select(study, subgroup, treatment, yi, vi) |>
  head()
```

```{r edss-fit, cache = TRUE}
edss_es <- escalc(measure = "IRR", yi = yi, vi = vi, data = edss)
fit_edss <- cams(edss_es, reference = "Lower", method = "REML")
```

```{r edss-forest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
forestplot(fit_edss, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## COVID-19 IL-6 antagonists: `il6`

Some trials report only one corticosteroid subgroup (as for **`steroids`**
in [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html)). Drop **`n = 0`** rows before
**`escalc()`**; use **`ifrac()`** / **`cams()`** on the completed table.

```{r il6-pattern}
il6_obs <- il6 |>
  filter(n > 0)
table(il6_obs$study, il6_obs$subgroup)
```

```{r il6-fit, cache = TRUE}
il6_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events,
  bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events,
  di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = il6_obs
)
fit_il6 <- cams(il6_es, reference = "no", method = "REML")
```

```{r il6-forest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
forestplot(fit_il6, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## RESPIRE: `respire_age` and `respire_sex`

Log hazard ratios and variances are precomputed from published intervals
(use trial-specific **`ci_level`** when converting from HR tables).

```{r respire-age-fit, cache = TRUE}
fit_ra <- cams(
  escalc(measure = "GEN", yi = respire_age$yi, vi = respire_age$vi, data = respire_age),
  reference = "<65",
  method = "REML"
)
```

```{r respire-sex-fit, cache = TRUE}
fit_rs <- cams(
  escalc(measure = "GEN", yi = respire_sex$yi, vi = respire_sex$vi, data = respire_sex),
  reference = "Male",
  method = "REML"
)
```

```{r respire-forests, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
forestplot(fit_ra, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r respire-sex-forest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
forestplot(fit_rs, exponentiate = TRUE)
```
